clue.text: Most scanty? Stick with these pants

indicators.note: in British slang pants means rubbish or badly done, so the words before it are botched into a new order

explanation.surface: A pun on sketchy underwear: a jab at some skimpy pants worn with a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like underwear (in British use, briefs) but is the slang adjective for 'rubbish', the anagram signal on STICK and THESE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sketchy means thin or lacking detail, so the superlative is a fair stand-in for the most meagre.

clue.text: A place to sit until now cuts bottom

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom is the last letter, and this phrase says that letter is chopped off

parts.note: so far means up to this point in time

explanation.surface: Someone sitting too long until their seat wears through at the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts bottom' removes the final R of SO FAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A couch or settee is furniture for sitting on, so the description fits plainly.

clue.text: Just fairly skilful, with central energy rising to the top

indicators.note: in a down clue rising to the top sends that letter up to the first position

parts.note: fairly means quite, as in quite good
a skilful person is able
E is the physics symbol for energy, and it sits at the very centre of the nine letters

explanation.surface: A judgement on someone fairly competent whose energy rises to the top.
explanation.walkthrough: QUITE ABLE has its central E sent up by 'rising to the top'; 'Just' is the adjective, not the adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Just as an adjective means fair and impartial, the same sense as even-handed treatment.

clue.text: Demand one eats shellfish? Just the opposite

indicators.note: eating puts one thing inside another
this reverses the roles so the shellfish swallows the one rather than the other way about

parts.note: a clam is a bivalve shellfish
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A demand that someone eat shellfish, then a reversal of who eats whom.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as written, I would contain CLAM; 'Just the opposite' turns it round so CLAM holds I.
explanation.definitionFit: To claim something is to insist on it as a right, a synonym of demand as a verb or noun.

clue.text: Trendy bars? One's not appreciative

parts.note: in means fashionable
a grate is a frame of metal bars

explanation.surface: Someone in fashionable bars who fails to show any gratitude.
explanation.definitionFit: An ungrateful person is one who does not appreciate kindness shown to them.

clue.text: Bottle's alcoholic substances

definitions.meaning: bottle is British slang for courage or nerve, and high morale or mettle is a person's pluck
strong distilled drinks such as gin and whisky

explanation.surface: A description of what a bottle holds: strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'bottle' means nerve, as in 'losing your bottle'; the 's reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural nouns for both courage and mood, and distilled liquor like brandy or rum.

clue.text: Clothes to boast about

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to brag is to boast

explanation.surface: Someone showing off about their outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is a word for dress or attire, a collective term for what one wears.

clue.text: Friendship? Girl embraces it

indicators.note: embracing wraps arms round, so the name goes around the other word

parts.note: Amy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl hugging something as a gesture of friendship.
explanation.definitionFit: Amity is friendly relations or goodwill between people or nations.

clue.text: Adults are moved behind black railing

indicators.note: in a down clue the reworked letters sit below, that is behind, the abbreviation

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: the letters are moved about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Grown-ups being shifted behind a dark railing.
explanation.definitionFit: A balustrade is a row of balusters topped by a rail, as along a staircase or balcony.

clue.text: Creature of myth beginning to alarm all the animals

parts.note: a faun is a Roman rural god, half man and half goat

indicators.note: the beginning of the following word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A mythical beast whose arrival starts to alarm every animal around.
explanation.definitionFit: Fauna is the collective term for the animal life of a region.

clue.text: Philosopher follows main point about run — it's grinding

indicators.note: the philosopher comes after the rest
about here means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: the gist is the essence of something
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
John Stuart Mill was a 19th-century English philosopher

explanation.surface: A philosopher pursuing a central argument, which proves a hard slog.
explanation.definitionFit: A gristmill is a mill for grinding grain into flour, so it is the thing doing the grinding.

clue.text: Entertaining swinger's hang-out?

parts.note: a circus acrobat who swings to entertain hangs from this bar, punning on a swinger's haunt

explanation.surface: Where a party-loving swinger likes to hang out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swinger' suggests a lively socialite and 'hang-out' a haunt; read literally, it is the bar a circus performer hangs from.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is a horizontal bar on ropes used by circus acrobats who swing from it.

clue.text: Source of the biggest hits of the Proms?

definitions.text: Source of the biggest hits of the Proms?

parts.words: Source of the biggest hits of the Proms?
parts.note: the hits are literal strikes on drums in an orchestra, not chart successes

explanation.surface: Asking which pieces are the most popular at the Proms concerts.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are a summer season of BBC classical concerts in London; the 'biggest hits' are the loudest drum strokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Kettledrums are the orchestral percussion that produce the loudest beats in a symphony orchestra.

clue.text: Charlie's trapped by ravine

indicators.note: trapping holds something inside, so the short word is enclosed

parts.note: a charlie is British slang for a fool, as is an ass; the 's reads as 'has'

explanation.surface: Someone called Charlie caught out by a deep gorge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' looks like a name but is slang for a fool; 'Charlie's trapped' means the fool has trapped the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss is a seemingly bottomless chasm, close in sense to a deep gorge.

clue.text: Light from Beth's ring's shimmering

indicators.note: shimmering suggests a wavering, unsettled state, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Light catching Beth's ring as it shimmers.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiance or luminosity is the quality of light, a noun sense matching the clue word.

clue.text: Big car smashed poodle's tail bones

indicators.note: a smashed car is broken up, so its letters are rearranged
the tail of the word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A big car crash that hurts a poodle's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The thorax's framework of ribs is a set of bones, a collective noun for skeleton parts.

clue.text: Draw a model of car on paper

parts.note: the Model T was an early Ford car
a tract is a short pamphlet or paper on a subject

explanation.surface: Instructions to sketch a model car on a sheet of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' suggests sketching but means to pull in; 'on' just places one piece next to the next.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a crowd is to pull it in, exactly the sense of lure or entice.

clue.text: Small crew with the Queen's ship

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a crew is a team working together
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A small crew sailing with the monarch's vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamer is a steamship, a vessel driven by steam power.

clue.text: Make a mess of surreal images chap's collected

indicators.note: being collected means being gathered inside, so the man goes within the rearranged letters
something surreal is distorted and dreamlike, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a chap is a man; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A man gathering bizarre surrealist pictures and bungling the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surreal' sounds like art criticism but is the anagram signal; 'chap's collected' reads as 'the chap is collected', so he is gathered inside the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To mismanage is to handle something badly, a direct synonym of botching.

clue.text: Welcomed desire to catch Spielberg film

indicators.note: catching holds something within, so the film goes inside

parts.note: greed is an excessive desire
E.T. is Steven Spielberg's 1982 film about an extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: Fans greeted keen to see a Spielberg film.
explanation.definitionFit: To be greeted is to be received with a hello, the past tense matching the clue word.

clue.text: Protection from French dealer in stolen goods

parts.note: de is the French word for from
a fence is a criminal who buys and sells stolen property

explanation.surface: Seeking protection from a French receiver of stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A defence is a means of guarding against attack, the British spelling of the noun.

clue.text: Happy to let in Penny, twice

indicators.note: the letting word goes in between the two pennies

parts.note: a penny is P in decimal money and D in old pre-1971 British money, so it gives both abbreviations
to lease property is to let it out

explanation.surface: Someone glad to let Penny in on two occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: Britain's old penny was written d (from Latin denarius) before decimal money brought p in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleased means content or glad, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Ideal school monitor, twisted about inside

indicators.note: twisted means turned round, so the two letters for about are flipped
the turned letters are those found inside the monitor's title

parts.note: a prefect is a senior pupil given duties
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An ideal head pupil who has gone a bit crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives the Latin-derived 're' (concerning); 'twisted' flips those two letters where they already sit 'inside' the monitor's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfect means flawless or ideal, an adjective matching the clue word.

clue.text: Roman finally wearing appropriate clothing for kingdom

indicators.note: something worn sits within the clothing, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a toga is the garment fitting for a Roman

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Roman at last dressed properly for a royal realm.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is a Pacific island nation ruled by a monarch.

clue.text: Sound from piano is excruciating

indicators.note: from signals that the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A painful din coming from a terrible piano player.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise is any sound, especially a loud or unpleasant one.

clue.text: Flour ma ordered for recipe

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Mum buying flour to bake from a recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A formula is a set method or list of ingredients for making something.

clue.text: Article removed from dirty relative

indicators.note: the article is taken out of the longer word

parts.note: unclean means dirty
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A filthy family member stripped of an article of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's brother is a family member, one of a person's kin.

clue.text: Stroked fabric

definitions.meaning: touched or handled, the past tense of the verb
a matted cloth made by pressing wool fibres together

explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of the touching verb, and the compressed woollen cloth used for hats.

clue.text: Former lover is conservative in belief, mainly — that's life

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes inside the shortened belief
mainly means most of it, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a tenet is a principle or belief

explanation.surface: An ex who stays conservative in outlook, which is just how life goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' trims TENET to TENE, and C goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Existence means being alive, so it is a fair synonym for being in the world.

clue.text: Long for clubs and wild party

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
a rave is a large lively dance party

explanation.surface: Pining for nightclubs and a wild party.
explanation.definitionFit: To crave something is to desire or yearn for it intensely.

clue.text: Predicts AS levels regularly falling

indicators.note: letters falling out at regular intervals leaves every other one of the phrase

explanation.surface: A forecast that A-level results will keep dropping.
explanation.walkthrough: AS levels are British exams usually taken around age 17; 'regularly falling' drops every other letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A seer sees the future, so foretelling is a recognised sense of the verb.

clue.text: Local community's payment arrangement

definitions.meaning: a village or colony where people have made their home
the settling of a debt or an agreed payout

explanation.definitionFit: A small inhabited place, and the agreed paying off of money owed.
